title: Slow-cooker chicken tacos
subtitle: Shredded spiced chicken for loading into taco shells
excerpt: Chicken thighs cooked with tomatoes, garlic, and Tex-Mex spices until pull-apart tender. Shred and pile into corn tacos with your choice of toppings.
sourceNotes: Shredded chicken tacos are a staple of Tex-Mex and Mexican-American home cooking. The slow-cooker method produces a very moist result. Adapted from standard American slow-cooker taco recipes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the shredded chicken in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat in a pan.
recipe.batchNotes: Excellent batch-cook filling. Make double and refrigerate for 4 days. Suits tacos, burritos, and jacket potatoes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the chicken a day ahead and refrigerate. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water and serve in warmed shells.

content.text: Chicken thighs are better than breast for tacos. They are fattier, stay moist over a long cook, and shred more evenly. The tinned tomatoes break down into a light sauce that the chicken absorbs as it shreds, which keeps everything moist and well seasoned.

Taco night is as much about the toppings as the filling. Set out whatever you have: soured cream, grated cheese, sliced jalapeños, shredded lettuce, diced tomato, spring onion, or fresh coriander. Warm the shells briefly under the grill or in a dry pan.

Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes, {{onion}} diced onion, and {{garlic}} of crushed garlic to the slow cooker. Add the spices: {{cumin-ground}} of cumin, {{chilli-powder}} of chilli powder, {{smoked-paprika}} of smoked paprika, {{garlic-powder}} of garlic powder, and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Stir to combine. Place {{chicken-thighs-boneless}} of chicken thighs in the sauce.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 5 to 6 hours. The chicken should shred very easily with two forks. Shred it directly in the pot and stir it through the sauce. Squeeze in {{lime}} lime juice and taste for seasoning.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry frying pan for 30 seconds each side, or wrap them in foil and heat in the oven at 180°C for 10 minutes. Pile the shredded chicken into the shells and top as you like.

rows.cause: The chicken and tomatoes released more liquid than expected.
rows.fix: Use a slotted spoon to lift the shredded chicken out of excess liquid. Stir in just enough of the liquid to moisten. Or reduce the liquid in a pan and spoon it back over.

rows.symptom: The chicken is not shredding easily
rows.cause: Not cooked long enough, or the thighs are very large.
rows.fix: Cook for a further 30 to 60 minutes on LOW. The chicken should fall apart when pressed with a fork.

rows.cause: The spices have cooked for a long time without blooming in oil, which can mute their impact.
rows.fix: Squeeze in more lime juice. Add a pinch of smoked paprika and cumin to the shredded filling and stir well before serving.

rows.symptom: The corn shells crack when filling them
rows.cause: Corn tortillas are fragile and need to be warm to flex without breaking.
rows.fix: Warm them for longer, or use two small shells overlapping per taco to give more structure.

content.text: Shredded chicken tacos are a standard of American Tex-Mex home cooking. They crossed into British kitchens in the 1990s alongside the growth of supermarket Mexican ingredients. The slow-cooker version is now one of the most-made taco recipes at home. It suits weeknights because the slow cooker does the work during the day.
